title: Prime Agents receive an automatic upkeep rebate for holding other Prime Agents' tokens
content:
A.6.1.1.8.2.3.2.2.1.1 states the Upkeep Rebate Primitive's whole substance: "Every Prime Agent is entitled to the Upkeep Rebate Primitive for tokens of other Prime Agents that they hold."

Read against the fee it offsets — 0.50% of market capitalization — the rebate's purpose becomes legible as a fix for double-counting. If Agent A holds Agent B's tokens, that holding is part of what the market prices into A's own market cap, while B is already paying upkeep on the same underlying value. Without a rebate, cross-holdings would be taxed twice, and the effective fee rate would rise with every layer of inter-Agent ownership.

The consequence is an incentive, not merely a correction. Because the rebate reduces a real USDS outflow, holding other Prime Agents' tokens is cheaper than holding equivalent value in any other form. The ecosystem is deliberately making Agents each other's shareholders, which knits their fortunes together — a Prime Agent has a direct financial interest in other Prime Agents succeeding.

The reflexive risk is the mirror image: mutual cross-holding also correlates Agent balance sheets, so a downturn in one Prime Agent propagates to every Agent holding it, at the same time as their own rebates shrink.
description: The entitlement applies to every Prime Agent by right, reducing fees in proportion to cross-held Agent tokens — value already taxed once at another Agent is not taxed again in full.
